note: X reads the painting's inscription as printed ('茅簷閒杵臼竹屋細 簸颺照人珠琲光奮…'); Y invents a different poem ('嘉穀既升盤 功需在簸揚…').

X's Greek has sense-changing misreadings that Y gets right as printed ('ἄγγελα δῆριν' for 'ἄγρια', 'ἐθιμόντε' for 'ἰθύνοντα', 'πυθέωσιν' for 'πτολίεσσιν'), and X's Latin has 'Belgicatum' for 'Belgica tum'.
The body texts agree in substance; Y has small slips ('eratérem', 'cam trado') and cuts the side note down to 'Agenoris filius.', where the print has 'Cadmus Agenoris filius'.
X reads 'magnus ille & spuriæ philosophiæ…spuriæ Deus', repeating 'spuriæ'; the print has 'totius philosophiæ', as Y gives it.
Y drops the title 'M. VITRVVII POLLIONIS DE ARCHITECTVRA LIBER SEXTVS. PRAEFATIO.' and puts 'f' where the print has long s ('fperemus'); X records the leaf faithfully.
X misreads every C as L, so the gathering references come out as 'L 3' instead of 'C 3' and the chapters as 'La./Lap.'; Y reads them correctly.

Y follows the printed apparatus (e.g. note a: 'Infra in itin. A. et B. خان روان ut Edrisi… D. خان زوان… E. خاوران ut Djih.-Numa'); X scrambles which manuscripts give which readings in notes a, b and d.
The two are nearly identical; Y has 'navigio pertransit' where the print has 'pertransitur'.
Both give only the ink shelfmark '12. 32. H. 5' and treat the mirrored title page as show-through.
Y leaves out passages ('sesquilatera longitudine ad Ciconiæ rostrum, colore'; 'iis, quas Gallinulas aquaticas … Germanis'), reads 'hominem' for 'nomen', and mixes line numbers into the text.
